{{Top|leg|notoc=1}}
A '''schizoid personality''' was a mental illness that could develop from psychological trauma, such as [[Torture/Legends|torture]].<ref name="Harm">{{DarkStryder|adventure=Harm's Way|book=The Kathol Rift}}</ref>

[[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Lowen Chase]] developed a schizoid personality at the hands of [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Langstyn Kraay]]. The mental torture he endured led to the development of paranoid delusions and egotism.<ref name="Harm" /> This condition had gone unnoticed by the crew of the ''[[FarStar]]'', but Chase gradually became more outspoken and insubordinate. Eventually, the full extent of his paranoia was made known when he organized a mutiny against [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Kaiya Adrimetrum]]. He became unstable and would rant and demonstrate impulsive behavior.<ref name="RE">{{DarkStryder|adventure=Rogue Elements|book=The Kathol Rift}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The depiction of [[Wikipedia:Schizoid personality disorder|schizoid personality]] in ''[[The Kathol Rift]]'', printed in [[May]] of [[1996]] by [[West End Games]], differs significantly in diagnostic criteria and symptomology of the real-world disorder. A diagnosis of schizoid personality disorder involves a pervasive pattern of social detachment, and restricted expression of emotions. An individual with this condition would begin to develop it in early adulthood and be seen by others as a "loner."<ref name="Schizoid">{{WebCite|url=http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmedhealth/PMH0001918|text=Schizoid personality disorder|work=PubMed Health|archivedate=20110210182844}}</ref>

Schizoid personality disorder does not include the paranoid delusions or the grandiose pattern of thinking that are present in Lowen Chase. These symptoms are more akin to [[Wikipedia:Schizotypal personality disorder|schizotypal personality disorder]], which is marked by cognitive or perceptual distortions and eccentric behavior. These eccentricities can include paranoid ideation and odd beliefs that influence behavior.<ref name="Schizotypal">{{WebCite|url=http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmedhealth/PMH0002493|text=Schizotypal personality disorder|work=PubMed Health|archivedate=20110216153224}}</ref>
